wa_north_cascades.blurb: The North Cascades of Washington are a rugged, glaciated range reached along Highway 20, in the country around North Cascades National Park. The terrain is a high plateau of summits cut by deep gorges rather than a single ridge, and the west side is wet and mossy while the east is hotter and drier. Most climbing here is alpine: long approaches, snow, and rock routes on summits, with a large share of class 3 and 4 scrambling and mountaineering and a smaller helping of trad and sport. Technical grades run from 5.4 up to 5.13, mostly 5.8 to 5.11. Washington Pass is the busiest zone, with granite spires that climb best from late June through September. The Picket Range and Chilliwack Range add more alpine terrain.

mi_marquette_and_central_up_roped.blurb: Marquette sits on the Lake Superior shore in Michigan's Upper Peninsula, and its roped climbing is spread over many small crags in the surrounding hills and along the lakeshore. The climbing is varied: sport routes make up the largest share, followed by trad, boulders and top-ropes, with a little ice in winter. Most routes fall between 5.7 and 5.12, with the heaviest concentration around 5.10, plus easy boulder problems. Cliffs can reach about 80 feet. Big areas include 550 Roped, Palmer, Big Bay and Presque Isle, and boulders sit right at the lake edge. Summer is the main season for rock, while frozen waterfalls and slopes draw ice climbers in the cold months.

ca_shuteye_ridge.blurb: Shuteye Ridge is a sprawling backcountry climbing region on the western slope of the southern Sierra Nevada, above Bass Lake and North Fork and south of Yosemite. Granite domes and walls rise out of the forest, with hard, highly featured rock: knobs, edges, cracks and water grooves. Sport and trad are almost evenly split, with a few boulders and top-ropes. Grades run mostly from 5.7 to 5.12, with the bulk of routes in the 5.10s and 5.11s, and terrain from low-angle slab to steep overhanging faces. Big Sleep, Chilkoot Lake, High Eagle and Shuteye Creek are the larger zones. Fall and spring are best; snow limits the season and summers are hot. The area is quiet and remote.

qc_08_abitibi_temiscamingue.blurb: Abitibi-Temiscamingue is a large, thinly populated region of western Quebec, so crags are far apart and a car is needed to link them. Climbing clusters around Amos, Rouyn-Noranda and Ville-Marie. Sport routes lead the way, with a solid amount of trad, some boulders and a few top-ropes. Most routes fall between 5.7 and 5.12, with the heaviest concentration in the 5.10s. Dalquier, near Amos, is a small chain of hills with a view over the Abitibi plain and routes of roughly 9 to 25 metres. Kekeko and Guidou, close to Rouyn-Noranda, are the other big venues, and Cotemis and the Chibekana cave sit near Ville-Marie.

nb_cochrane_lane_cliffs.blurb: Cochrane Lane Cliffs, near Welsford in southern New Brunswick, is the largest concentration of routes in the province. The rock is mostly pink granite of generally good quality, though a few spots are less solid. Climbing is predominantly trad, with a fair number of bolted and mixed-gear routes. Routes run from about 30 to 200 feet and are mostly single pitch, though several can be linked into a longer outing. Grades span 5.5 to 5.12, with the greatest weight in the 5.9 to 5.11 range. Walls and areas include The Upper Tier, Joe's Garage, The Dawn Walls and Minkey Wall. It tends to be quiet and often nearly empty on weekdays.

bc_murrin_park.blurb: Murrin Park is a cluster of granite crags just south of Squamish, tucked among trees close to Browning Lake. Trad and sport routes dominate, with trad somewhat ahead, and there is a good set of boulders as well. Grades run from about 5.7 to 5.13, with the heaviest concentration at 5.10 and plenty at 5.11 and 5.12. Styles are varied: easy slabs, trad lines at most grades, big overhangs, long vertical sport routes and test-piece cracks. Most cliffs face east, so they are shaded on hot afternoons, and some are quiet even when the park is busy. Petrifying Wall, Splitsville, Lakeside in the Woods and the Missing Boulders are among the larger zones.
